findings.title: Invalidate existing local recovery codes when replacing them in user storage
findings.body: When updateCredential succeeds in external storage, this method leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential untouched. This occurs for users who configured recovery codes before their storage provider supported storing them externally. Regenerating their codes now saves a new external set without revoking the old local set, which can still be accepted by local credential validation when external validation fails. Remove the superseded local recovery credential after successfully storing the replacement externally, and test that codes from the previous local set no longer authenticate.

findings.title: Exercise consumption of externally stored recovery codes
findings.body: The new recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted code occurs in the original list; it never consumes a successful code or updates its position. getCredentials also recreates a fresh credential from that unchanged list on every call. Consequently, this fixture permits unlimited reuse, always presents the first code, and never exercises the authenticator's exhausted-code handling. The new integration test logs in only once, so it passes despite these violations of the recovery-code lifecycle. Implement consumption in the fixture and test replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.
